issue.title: docs/xprompt.md's bundled-skills table omits sase_monitor and sase_new_task, two of the most-invoked bundled skills
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY phase bead sase-p8.5 (epic sase-p8, 'sase pipe'), routed here by that epic's land agent. NOT caused by that epic: sase-p8.5 added the sase_pipe row to this table and noticed the two pre-existing gaps while doing so.

WHAT IS WRONG: the bundled-skills table in docs/xprompt.md (around line 1172, the '| ... | ... |' table that begins with sase_agents_status) lists 17 of the 19 bundled skill sources under src/sase/xprompts/skills/. Missing rows: sase_monitor and sase_new_task. Verified by diffing the table's first column against 'ls src/sase/xprompts/skills/' — every other source has a row, including the sase_pipe row just added.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TYPICAL DOC GAP: these are not obscure skills. sase_monitor is the mandated replacement for provider-native background execution, and sase_new_task is mandatory before creating any task bead — both are named as required workflow steps in the project's own agent instructions. A reader consulting the canonical table of bundled skills to learn what exists will not find either one. docs/xprompt.md itself references '/sase_new_task' in prose twice (the #bd/land_epic and epic-worker rows near lines 1267 and 1301) without the table entry that would explain it.

SCOPE: add the two rows in alphabetical position with one-line descriptions matching each source's frontmatter description, in the style of the surrounding rows. While there, consider whether the table should be generated from the skill sources instead of hand-maintained — it has now drifted at least three times, and a test comparable to tests/main/test_init_skills_sources.py's enumeration could pin it.

payload.close_reason: Fixed: the bundled-skills table in docs/xprompt.md now carries both missing rows -- `sase_monitor` at line 1276 and `sase_new_task` at line 1277 -- with one-line descriptions matching their frontmatter. Verified 2026-08-24 at 45806495f.
